guide.summary: Forgejo documents an Authorization Code OAuth2 provider with PKCE, and its tokens are accepted as Bearer tokens on the API. The documented OAuth tokens are unscoped: scopes are not implemented, so a token can run any action on behalf of the user. The read-only and no-create/edit/delete limits must be enforced by the app, not by the token. Repository listing can use the /api/v1/repos/search endpoint with page and limit pagination. The OAuth API security list in the supplied Swagger snapshot does not name OAuth explicitly, so bearer use on that endpoint remains unconfirmed.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for List repository names visible to the connected person, including pagination. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: Register an OAuth2 application on each customer instance before testing
findings.detail: The Authorization Code grant requires registering an application in the user's settings at /user/settings/applications. Any user can register one there. Each customer instance needs its own client registration and redirect configuration before a first test can run.
findings.appliesWhen: Every customer instance that connects through OAuth

evidence.quote: OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test

It is possible for any user to manually register a new OAuth2 application on the /user/settings/applications page for the purpose of using Git credential helpers different from the pre-registered ones.

findings.title: Use the Authorization Code grant with PKCE and send the token as a Bearer header
findings.detail: Forgejo supports the Authorization Code grant with PKCE for public clients and confidential clients. The access token from the token endpoint is accepted in the Authorization Bearer header for API requests on the user's behalf.
findings.appliesWhen: Individual customer accounts authorizing the app against their own instance

evidence.quote: Supported OAuth2 Grants At the moment, Forgejo only supports the Authorization Code Grant standard with additional support for the following extensions:
Authorization: Bearer ... header in HTTP headers
Use the access_token to make API requests to access the user’s resources.

findings.title: OAuth tokens are unscoped and can act as the user across all actions
findings.detail: OAuth2 scopes are not implemented. Tokens can execute any action on behalf of the user, not only Git actions. The app must enforce read-only behavior itself. A passage also states that third-party apps that obtain tokens through instance-wide admin-created applications have administrative rights; that passage does not establish the boundary for user-registered applications.
findings.appliesWhen: Any OAuth token used for the repository listing action

evidence.quote: OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.
execute any actions on behalf of the user, not just Git-related actions.
Note Third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via such an application will have administrative rights.

findings.title: Connected person must already be able to see the repositories being listed
findings.detail: Visibility follows the connected user's existing account access. The OAuth token adds no separate repository-level grant, so the account must be checked to see the repositories that the listing should return.
findings.appliesWhen: Customer accounts that already have repository access on their instance

evidence.quote: Parameter private in query (boolean, optional): include private repositories this user has access to (defaults to true)
## GET /api/v1/repos/search | Search for repositories

steps.title: Register an OAuth2 application on the customer's Forgejo instance
steps.detail: Each customer instance needs its own OAuth2 application registered at /user/settings/applications with the app's redirect URI. Record the Client ID and Client secret for the token exchange. Use a public client with PKCE or a confidential client, per the documentation.
steps.doneWhen: The customer instance shows an OAuth2 application with a Client ID and redirect URI configured for this app.

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: After the customer authorizes the app at /login/oauth/authorize, exchange the returned code at the token endpoint using the documented JSON body. This is an unexecuted authorization step; the grant_type is the documented constant authorization_code.
steps.doneWhen: The token endpoint returns an access_token with token_type bearer for the authorizing user.

steps.title: List accessible repositories, first page
steps.detail: Call the repository search endpoint with limit and page, sending the OAuth access token as a Bearer header. The private parameter defaults to true, so private repositories the connected person can access are included. Read the returned list and identify the field that holds each repository name from the response schema before extracting names; do not assume a wrapper key. Capture the Link and X-Total-Count response headers for pagination. Boundary check: compare returned names with a private repository owned by another account that the connected person has not been granted; that name must not appear in the results. Issue only this GET request.
steps.doneWhen: The response returns 200 with a repository list, repository names are extracted using the schema field, and the Link and X-Total-Count headers are recorded. The denied repository name is absent from the results.

evidence.quote: Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is
Parameter private in query (boolean, optional): include private repositories this user has access to (defaults to true)
Parameter limit in query (integer, optional): page size of results

fields: <ACCESS_TOKEN>: access_token from the token exchange step
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash
limit=50: page size; must not exceed the max_response_items value from the instance API settings
<DENIED_REPO_FULL_NAME>: private repo the user cannot access, for boundary check

steps.title: Follow pagination until the last page
steps.detail: Follow the rel=next URL from each Link header exactly as returned, resolved on the same HTTPS instance host. Do not construct or edit URLs and do not add or change parameters. Repeat until a response has no Link header with rel=next, which the documentation describes as present only when more pages exist. Combine the repository names from all pages. Boundary check: confirm each page is a GET to the search endpoint with the same Bearer token and that the request log contains no POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE calls.
steps.doneWhen: No rel=next link remains in the last response, and the combined repository name count equals the X-Total-Count value from the first response.

steps.title: Request the next page of repository results
steps.detail: Continuation of the listing action: request each subsequent page by following the rel=next URL from the previous response, unchanged, until no rel=next link is returned. Boundary check: confirm every request in the outgoing log is a GET to the repository search endpoint and that no create, edit or delete calls were made.
steps.doneWhen: The final page returns without a rel=next Link header, and every page was retrieved by following the returned next URL.

blockers.title: Confirm bearer OAuth tokens are accepted on /api/v1/repos/search
blockers.resolution: Run the first listing request with a real OAuth token. If it returns 401, the Swagger snapshot's security list does not cover OAuth on this endpoint and the approach must be revisited.

blockers.title: Read-only behavior is not enforced by the token
blockers.resolution: OAuth2 scopes are not implemented, so the token can perform any action. The app must only issue GET requests to the listing endpoint and must not call create, edit or delete routes.

blockers.title: List repository names visible to the connected person, including pagination
blockers.resolution: The mapping to GET /api/v1/repos/search with Bearer auth and an empty permissions list is supported by the quoted unscoped OAuth grant and pagination sources, but the handoff is incomplete: list-repos-next-pages has dependsOn [] although it needs the Link header from list-repos-first-page, and list-repos-continuation-page duplicates the listing without a defined start, so the next-page steps should depend on list-repos-first-page and the duplicate should be removed or merged.

requirements.title: Connected person must already be able to see the repositories being listed
requirements.detail: Visibility follows the connected user's existing account access. The OAuth token adds no separate repository-level grant, so the account must be checked to see the repositories that the listing should return.
requirements.appliesWhen: Customer accounts that already have repository access on their instance

blockers.title: Confirm bearer OAuth tokens are accepted on /api/v1/repos/search
blockers.resolution: Run the first listing request with a real OAuth token. If it returns 401, the Swagger snapshot's security list does not cover OAuth on this endpoint and the approach must be revisited.

blockers.title: Read-only behavior is not enforced by the token
blockers.resolution: OAuth2 scopes are not implemented, so the token can perform any action. The app must only issue GET requests to the listing endpoint and must not call create, edit or delete routes.

blockers.title: List repository names visible to the connected person, including pagination
blockers.resolution: The mapping to GET /api/v1/repos/search with Bearer auth and an empty permissions list is supported by the quoted unscoped OAuth grant and pagination sources, but the handoff is incomplete: list-repos-next-pages has dependsOn [] although it needs the Link header from list-repos-first-page, and list-repos-continuation-page duplicates the listing without a defined start, so the next-page steps should depend on list-repos-first-page and the duplicate should be removed or merged.

details.title: Use the Authorization Code grant with PKCE and send the token as a Bearer header
details.detail: Forgejo supports the Authorization Code grant with PKCE for public clients and confidential clients. The access token from the token endpoint is accepted in the Authorization Bearer header for API requests on the user's behalf.
details.appliesWhen: Individual customer accounts authorizing the app against their own instance

evidence.quote: Supported OAuth2 Grants At the moment, Forgejo only supports the Authorization Code Grant standard with additional support for the following extensions:
Authorization: Bearer ... header in HTTP headers
Use the access_token to make API requests to access the user’s resources.

details.title: OAuth tokens are unscoped and can act as the user across all actions
details.detail: OAuth2 scopes are not implemented. Tokens can execute any action on behalf of the user, not only Git actions. The app must enforce read-only behavior itself. A passage also states that third-party apps that obtain tokens through instance-wide admin-created applications have administrative rights; that passage does not establish the boundary for user-registered applications.

preparation.title: Registration worksheet
preparation.text:
Register an OAuth2 application on the customer's Forgejo instance
Each customer instance needs its own OAuth2 application registered at /user/settings/applications with the app's redirect URI. Record the Client ID and Client secret for the token exchange. Use a public client with PKCE or a confidential client, per the documentation.
Fields: <INSTANCE_BASE_URL>: customer's full HTTPS Forgejo base URL, user-supplied, <CLIENT_ID>: returned after registering the application, <REDIRECT_URI>: the app's callback URL, set during registration

preparation.title: First connection test
preparation.text:
Exchange the authorization code for an access token
Done when: The token endpoint returns an access_token with token_type bearer for the authorizing user.

List accessible repositories, first page
Done when: The response returns 200 with a repository list, repository names are extracted using the schema field, and the Link and X-Total-Count headers are recorded. The denied repository name is absent from the results.

Follow pagination until the last page
Done when: No rel=next link remains in the last response, and the combined repository name count equals the X-Total-Count value from the first response.

Request the next page of repository results
Done when: The final page returns without a rel=next Link header, and every page was retrieved by following the returned next URL.
